title: Gaussian Elimination and Back Substitution
quickIdea: Reduce [A|b] by row operations until the coefficient part is in echelon form, count the pivots for the rank, read off any contradiction, then solve from the bottom row upwards.
remember: Work on [A|b], not on A alone: the right-hand side must undergo every row operation too.
The three elementary row operations are swapping two rows, multiplying a row by a non-zero scalar, and adding a multiple of one row to another. Each one preserves the solution set exactly.
In row echelon form the number of non-zero rows of the coefficient part is rank(A); the number of pivots in the whole augmented matrix is rank([A|b]).
A row that reads (0 0 ... 0 | c) with c not 0 is a contradiction and settles the question: no solution.
When there is no contradiction, back substitution starts at the last pivot and works upwards, expressing each pivot variable in terms of the free ones.
Do not use column operations to solve a system: they change the unknowns and therefore change the solution set.

example.prompt: Solve x + y = 3, x - y = 1 by elimination.
example.work: The augmented matrix is [[1,1,3],[1,-1,1]]. Replace row 2 by row 2 - row 1: [[1,1,3],[0,-2,-2]]. Back substitution: -2y = -2 gives y = 1, then x + 1 = 3 gives x = 2.
example.answer: x = 2, y = 1. Two pivots, rank(A) = rank([A|b]) = 2 = n, so the solution is unique.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 1998 Q.1.2 is solved in one step once the augmented matrix is written: row 2 - 4 row 1 produces (0 0 0 | -8) and the answer is immediate. GATE CSE 2003 Q.41 needs the last row of the reduced augmented matrix to be set to zero, which is a back-substitution-style reading of the parameter condition.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: After elimination the augmented matrix ends with the row (0 0 0 | 5). What does that tell you?
variations.why: The row asserts 0 = 5. Equivalently rank([A|b]) is one more than rank(A), so b lies outside the column space.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Elimination on a 3 x 3 system leaves two pivots and no contradictory row. How many solutions, and why?
variations.answer: Infinitely many, with one free parameter.
variations.why: rank(A) = rank([A|b]) = 2 < 3, so the nullity is 1 and the solution set is a line.

trap.what: Forgetting to apply a row operation to the augmented column, or using column operations to clear entries.
trap.why: The solution is a property of the pair (A, b). Changing only A breaks the correspondence, and column operations relabel or mix the unknowns, which is a different system.
trap.counterexample: Clearing the (2,1) entry of [[1,1],[1,-1]] by a column operation, column 1 - column 2, gives [[0,1],[2,-1]], a system whose solutions are not those of the original.

check.question: An augmented matrix in echelon form has three pivots in the coefficient part of a 4-unknown system, and no contradictory row. How many solutions?
check.answer: Infinitely many, with one free parameter.
check.explanation: rank(A) = rank([A|b]) = 3 while n = 4, so the nullity is 1 and the solution set is a line.
